chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Moalla ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Al-Najjashi proposed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for Amina, daughter of Abu Sufyan, and he married her, he called for food and said: "Indeed, among the Sunnah of the sent messengers is feeding people at the time of marriage."'

key_terms.سُنَنِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ: The traditions/customs of the sent messengers (Prophets)

ai.seo_question: What is the religious significance of hosting a meal during marriage in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) cites the proposal of Al-Najjashi for Amina bint Abi Sufyan as a precedent, where he hosted a meal to mark the occasion, declaring that feeding guests is a established Sunnah of the Prophets. This narration, found in al-Kafi, underscores the social and spiritual significance of communal dining in validating and celebrating marital unions within Shia tradition. It highlights the continuity of prophetic customs (Sunnah) in daily life, linking personal joy with communal gratitude.
